title: Why you should care about AI interpretability - Mark Bissell, Goodfire AI
talk_summary: Mark Bissell of Goodfire explains mechanistic interpretability—reverse-engineering model internals to find and steer features—and demos steering Llama to protect PII, dynamic prompting, and painting with image-model concepts. It is a vendor pitch for their Ember platform aimed at model developers, not agent-orchestration teams.

takeaways.what_they_do: They locate an internal 'sensitive/protected information' feature and amplify it ~60% to make the model refuse to leak an email, instead of prompt-editing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want to turn that up from its normal level to you know call it 60% more suddenly the model takes PII and sensitive information much more seriously

takeaways.technique: Dynamic/conditional prompt injection on detected intent
takeaways.what_they_do: They watch an internal feature (e.g. 'beverages') and inject a different system prompt mid-generation when it fires, rather than one static prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the feature for beverages and consumer brands starts to fire ... I'm actually going to inject a different prompt

takeaways.technique: Model diffs as a regression check after training
takeaways.what_they_do: They propose diffing which internal features changed after post-training to catch unwanted behavior drift before deploy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can almost do a git diff of what features have changed or evolved

takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest pruning weights a model doesn't need for a narrow task (e.g. a coding-only Claude) for efficiency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a version of Claude that only needs to perform coding and could you pair out a lot of its um, you know, a lot of its parameters
